Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 26
  gender: Male
  ethnicity: European
  relationship_status: Married
  occupation: Fisherman
  trauma_type: Torture
  pcl5: 37

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Triggers: Auditory (Babies): Babies, Public Transport: Bus riding, Feeling Vulnerable: Feeling emotionally vulnerable
  Threat: Back to Wall: I feel unsafe unless my back is against a wall where I can see the room, Intrusion Monitoring: I listen for sounds that might mean someone is entering my home, Noticing Weapons: I notice potential weapons or dangerous objects in any environment
  Memory: Rage on Recall: When I remember the event I feel intense rage, Bodily Reenactment: When memories come to mind of what happened, I feel my body is in the same position as when the frightening event occurred., Pain Recall: When the memory returns I feel physical pain in the same parts of my body as during the event

Vignette:
Tom, a 26-year-old European-American fisherman, has been struggling with intense psychological distress since his traumatic experience involving torture. His wife noticed that he had become increasingly withdrawn and seemed to be in constant fear. Tom’s journey towards seeking help began months after the event, but the memories of what happened continue to haunt him. Tom was working on a fishing vessel when he was captured by pirates who held him captive for several weeks. During this time, he endured relentless abuse and torture. The memory of his captors’ voices still evokes intense rage within him. Any auditory cues that remind him of those sounds—such as the cries of babies or the rumble of a bus—are enough to send him into a state of high alert. Back on land, Tom found himself constantly feeling unsafe unless his back was firmly against a wall where he could see everything around him. This need for control and visibility became a defining feature of his life. Even at home, he would frequently check the locks on doors and windows and listen intently for any sounds that might indicate an intruder. His heightened state of vigilance made it difficult to relax or feel safe in any environment. The physical sensations associated with the trauma were equally distressing. When memories surfaced, Tom felt his body reenact the positions he was forced into during the torture. The pain he experienced then came back vividly, often leaving him immobilized and unable to function normally. He would find himself frozen in place, reliving the agony of those moments. Tom’s daily life as a fisherman added another layer of complexity. The unpredictable nature of his work on the open sea made him feel vulnerable and exposed. The isolation and lack of control over his environment heightened his anxiety. He often avoided going out to sea alone, preferring to have someone with him even if it meant working longer hours or missing some fishing opportunities. His marriage was also strained by these experiences. Tom’s wife noticed that he had become distant and less affectionate. His constant need for safety measures at home made her feel as though she were living in a fortress rather than a shared space. The emotional vulnerability he felt made it difficult for him to open up about his fears, leading to a growing sense of isolation even within the confines of his marriage. Despite these challenges, Tom’s wife encouraged him to seek help after noticing how much his symptoms had escalated. She expressed concern about his mental health and urged him to find someone who could understand what he was going through. Initially reluctant, Tom finally agreed to see a therapist when he realized that his condition was affecting not only himself but also those around him. In therapy, Tom is most afraid of losing control and being vulnerable again. He hopes to regain a sense of safety and trust in the world. His main goal is to find ways to manage his triggers without feeling overwhelmed by the memories and physical sensations they evoke. Through this process, he aims to reconnect with his wife and return to a more normal life as a fisherman. Tom’s story is one of resilience and hope, even amidst the profound trauma he has endured. The therapist's role will be crucial in helping him navigate these fears and gradually build a sense of safety and trust once again.
